text: **Sub-phases (IDs unchanged).** The e6 and e8 splits are supported and described in §3. For e9, a split at about Jun/Jul 2026 fits better than one at Vivaldi. Note the e5/e6 overlap in Oct–Nov 2023, and that e9 in practice starts on 29 Jan 2026, not 1 Feb.

**Weapon dates still missing:**
  - NLAW's first delivery (UK, reportedly Jan 2022).
  - Abrams' and HIMARS' first combat-use dates.
  - Patriot's first intercept (the claimed Kinzhal kill of 4 May 2023). Ukrainska Pravda's 5 May item is an initial Air Force denial, and ISW's 6–7 May 2023 pages did not mention it.
  - Exact Leopard and Bradley combat debuts beyond "June 2023".
  - Oryx per-country F-16 attribution is approximate.
  - The Kiel heavy-weapons sheet was not parsed.

**Territory anchors.** The March 2022 peak occupied share is still unsourced. Euromaidan searches of June 2022 reporting found no usable figure. The end-2022 and end-2023 values in §1 are derived from DeepState yearly totals, not reported directly. The monthly series belongs to 07 §2.7.

**Contested 2026 area figures.**
  - Reuters' "600 km² by 8 Jun" figure (Syrskyi) could not be fetched (401) and is dropped.
  - The Vivaldi total ranges from 125 km² (the corps) to 200+ km² (analysts).
**US peace plan, Sep 2026.** CSMonitor says Zelensky rejected it. ISW says he agreed "fundamental principles" on 6 Sep. The plan's text has not been published.

**Iran war and the negotiation calendar.** Reports that the war postponed an Abu Dhabi/US-hosted round in March 2026 could not be confirmed from a fetched source. The exact start date of the war is also not independently sourced here.
**Glide-bomb monthly counts** from the Ukrainian Air Force (2024–2026) were not captured here; see 03.

**Russian FPV production for 2023–24.** No Ukrainian or Western estimate was found; only the SZRU's 2025 target of 2m exists. Russian claims were deliberately not used. The long-range production figures conflict: 79,000 Shahed-types a year (HUR) against 400+ a day (Syrskyi). Searched Kyiv Independent, Euromaidan Press and Militarnyi. RUSI and CSIS site searches did not render.

**Lancet strike counts after March 2023.** WarSpotting's Lancet tracker blocks scripted access, and its public API covers only Russian losses. Oryx stopped in March 2023, and the Russian LostArmour tally is excluded by the sourcing rules. The Air Force's 10,604 Lancets destroyed (to Aug 2026) is the only volume indicator. Lancet ranges after 2023 are reported only qualitatively.

**Shahed data before mid-2024 and after May 2026.** The compiled Air Force series is a floor for 2022–23, because some early reports gave only the number destroyed. From May 2026 the Air Force stopped publishing consistent counts, so ISIS figures for the later months are reconstructions. The dataset licence (CC BY-NC-SA) means it should be cited, not bundled.
**Kill-zone depth** is still commanders' estimates. No systematic measurement of the Russian band after February 2026 exists, beyond ISW's qualitative "reduced tempo and depth".

**Casualty-share figures.** The 60–70% (systems, RUSI) and 70–80% (casualties, Ukrainian officials via OSW, and damage in the 7th Corps sector) figures measure different things; none is audited, and Ukrainian casualties from Russian drones are poorly quantified.

**Hit rates.** These remain definition-dependent. RUSI's 60–80% failure rate, CSIS's 10–15% success without guidance, OSW's 30% → 70% accuracy and the USF's claim of roughly one target per five sorties are not comparable. No 2026 field study was found, and manufacturer interceptor rates (60–90%) are self-reported.

**Heavy bombers.** Vampire specs come from press relaying SkyFall; the maker's own site did not resolve. The Russian "Kashchei" was searched again and not found in any English-language outlet, so it is dropped. The Berdysh specs are relayed from Russian Telegram.
**Fixed-wing ISR costs** are not published by Deviro, Athlon Avia or Ukrspecsystems.

**Swarms.** Swarm use is small-scale (Swarmer's "over a hundred" missions by Sep 2025; CSIS calls it experimental). No adoption share for AI terminal guidance beyond the 10,000 bought in 2024 was found.

**Russian systems still thin.** Krasukha-2 in Ukraine, Pole-21 specs and Russian trench-jammer families beyond Volnorez have no fetched spec source. Militarnyi and Euromaidan site searches returned only loss reports; Defense Express's search is script-driven and could not be queried.
**Ukrainian systems.** Nota has no spec source beyond being named among the large vehicle systems pulled back from the front. Bukovel specs still rest on Wikipedia.

**Gun and passive defence over time.** No series of kill shares by weapon type (mobile fire groups, Gepard, Skynex, interceptors, EW) was found for 2022–26. We have only snapshots: EW about 50% (a Night Watch claim), interceptors more than 40% on one night, and jets outrunning mobile fire groups in 2026. Official totals lump kinetic and EW kills.
**Digital links.** The Russian switch to digital video is documented for Molniya only, and the Ukrainian digital or encrypted video share is unquantified.
**Firmware cadence.** It is quantified for DJI war firmware (more than 40 versions in two years) but not for DELTA, Kropyva or Ukrainian FPV firmware.
**Current FPV loss rates.** There is no 2026 equivalent of RUSI's 60–80% failure figure. RUSI's publication listings are script-driven and no 2026 RUSI tactical report was found.
**Starlink-cut effects.** The ISW 8 and 26 February assessments are now included (via Wayback). A common km² measure of the gains is still missing.

**Russian recovery.** Terminal types after the cut (Yamal/Express GEO terminals, bribed whitelist registrations at scale) have no fetched source. How much of Russia's pre-cut drone depth has returned by September 2026 is not measured.

**Artillery, HIMARS and glide bombs in Vivaldi and the southern counteroffensive.** No source quantifies them. Vivaldi was run under "maximum information silence", and the ISW special report and daily assessments (read via Wayback) describe drone-led shaping fires, not tube fire. A later RUSI fieldwork report is the likeliest source.

**Per-town KAB counts.** Avdiivka (February 2024) is sourced. Vovchansk has only qualitative reporting, and Kharkiv city only a strike count (more than 50 by mid-June 2024). ISW assessments from May–June 2024 via Wayback had no per-town numbers.

**KAB monthly series gaps.** February 2026 is derived (March minus "more than 1,500"). Most 2024 and 2025 months are missing; only April–May 2024, early 2025, October and November 2025 are sourced. A full Air Force/MoD series was not found in English.

**Artillery's share of casualties.** Only the complement is sourced: drones cause 70–80% (Latvian SAB), and more than 80% of targets destroyed (UA MoD). No source splits the remaining 20–30% between artillery, glide bombs, mines and small arms.

**Conflicting production figures.** RUSI's 70,000 UMPK ordered for 2025 against HUR's 120,000 planned. Actual drops (~44,000 in Jan–Nov 2025) suggest stockpiling or overstated plans. Flamingo's maker claims (30–210 a month) are contradicted by the strike record (~10 strikes). Sapsan's production is unverified.

**Czech initiative totals.** Pavel's figures differ between February 2026 (4.4M cumulative, almost 2M in 2025) and May 2026 (just over 3M: 1.5M plus 1.8M). The difference may be calibre scope (122 mm included) or counting method.

**Interceptor-drone kill share.** Official counts conflict (USF: over 1,200 in May 2026; Sting's maker: over 3,000), and the Air Force stopped publishing Shahed counts from May 2026. Cost per kill is only implied (a ~$2k interceptor against a $20–50k Shahed); file 01 has the detail.
**Ballistic intercept methodology.** CSIS, the MoD monthly and Air Force per-salvo figures are now all sourced, but none separates PAC-3 from SAMP/T or counts interceptors fired per kill.

**Ukrainian casualties remain opaque.** The range runs from Zelensky's 55,000 killed (Feb 2026) through UALosses' named count (about 97,000 dead and 98,000 missing, June 2026) to CSIS's 100–140k. Kyiv publishes no wounded figure after Zelensky's February 2025 statement of 380,000. The missing blur the split between killed and wounded.

**Russian totals still diverge.** They range from about 259,000 named dead (Mediazona/BBC), through 500,000 killed (UK intelligence), to about 1.53M killed and wounded (Ukrainian General Staff). The only KIA:WIA trend found is a low-reliability columnist's derivation from General Staff data.

**Ukrainian manpower reform is in flux.** Whether the June 2026 contract "experiment" becomes law is unknown: Syrskyi questioned its legal basis, and the defence minister who launched it has been dismissed. No figures were found for the AWOL return scheme's uptake or for compliance with the 60-day rotation target. AWOL totals conflict: Euromaidan says "more than 100,000" cumulative, while Fedorov said about 200,000 in January 2026.

**Minefield density per km** for 2023 versus 2024–26 was not found. The RUSI reports, Euromaidan and ISW give only qualitative descriptions (systematic Russian seeding, remote mining) and unit claims such as 200 m a day. No UN or HALO figure for mined area was fetched; the two official Ukrainian figures (133,300 km² affected, 4,600 km² requiring clearance) measure different things.
**UGV casevac success rate.** No success or failure percentage was found, only anecdotes (four UGVs for one casualty) and RUSI's early-2025 verdict that the systems were unreliable.

**Battles still thin.** Euromaidan reports on the later Vovchansk fighting (2025–26) and on the September 2024 recapture of the aggregate plant were found but not added. Kurakhove rests on one DeepState/ISW summary. Rubikon's role at Huliaipole is unconfirmed.
**North Korean primary sources.** South Korean NIS statements were reached only through Yonhap and OSW secondary reports; 38 North, NK News (paywalled) and France24 (403) could not be read.

**Search limits.** The web-search budget was exhausted before this pass, so sources came from Euromaidan's WordPress search API, Kyiv Independent tag pages, and links inside fetched pages. The ISW page was read through a Wayback Machine snapshot.

**How far Russia's C2 recovered, in numbers.** The pattern is clear: a 20–40% drop in February, partial substitutes by mid-March, and "gradually restored" C2 by August. But nobody has published a measured comparison of Russian drone sorties or strike depth before and after. ISW's daily assessments stop discussing Starlink after March. We sampled the April–May assessments and found no further Starlink passages, and could not read June–September systematically because Wayback throttles access.
**Vivaldi's full scope.** Only two of four "seasons" are public. The size of the area is disputed (125+ km² claimed against mappers' 200–240 km²), and losses are corps claims.
**Jet-powered Gerans and interceptor drones.** Not covered here in depth; see 01/02/03. Their effect on Ukrainian rail and energy logistics in 2026 still needs a figure.

**Kill-zone depth varies by sector.** The estimates (15, 20–25, 25+, 15–30 km) come from different commanders and methods. Mission Control holds strike data by depth band, but no map or dataset is public.

**UGV loss rates army-wide.** We have one commander's lifespan figures (12–15 → 3–4 missions) and road counts (10+, 50+ wrecks), but no MoD loss or failure share. The "90% of a regiment's deliveries by UGV" claim is still unverified.

**Detection-to-strike latency in 2025–26.** Still no independent measurement of the Ukrainian loop. The available figures are Russian developer claims (via CSIS), unattributed media figures and MoD claims. No RUSI or CSIS fieldwork number for 2025–26 turned up in the RUSI and CSIS catalogues.
**Russian rail versus truck share and depot distances in 2026.** No systematic figure. We have only anecdotes: a 400 km fuel run, a repair base moved 250 km back, M-14 freight down 71%.

**Figures that conflict:**
  - The start of the southern counteroffensive: the Air Assault Forces and Euromaidan Press give 29 January [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-quiet-counteroffensive], and ISW first observed counterattacks on 9 February. The often-quoted 11 February traces back to Wikipedia (see 00 §3 e9).
  - Jamestown converts UAH 5 billion to "$1.12 million". The MoD figure is UAH 5bn, which Euromaidan Press gives as about $112 million, so Jamestown slipped by a factor of 100 [src:mod-2026-logistics-lockdown-launch].

**Soviet belt design norms.** Spacing as multiples of tree height and the official cross-belt rules were still not found. The measured grid (§2.7) and Parfonov now replace the search-only Oleshky figure as the basis. The forestry-journal site refused connections again, the MDPI Ukraine shelterbelt papers (Land 2025, Resources 2025) returned 403, and Ukrainian-language norms were out of scope.

**Measurement coverage.** Five boxes is a small sample, and OSM completeness varies. The next step is to run the same method over the NASA Harvest field polygons offline (NC-ND, statistics only) or over a belt layer derived from WorldCover or Dynamic World.
**Balka dimensions.** No source gives typical balka widths, depths or slope angles. Measure them from Copernicus GLO-30 along the sample boxes. Chalk hills beyond the Sviati Hory area are unsourced.

**Weather effects.** Rain, fog and icing are now sourced qualitatively. Wind limits, summer dust and any *quantified* foliage-versus-detection relationship were not found. Parfonov says only that canopy "substantially" degrades FPV effectiveness, and a Resources 2025 paper mentions rising dust storms without figures.

**Crater density 2023–26.** No crater-density study for Donbas or Zaporizhzhia after 2022 was found. The Kyinska hromada count (e1) lacks an area, so it gives no density. UNOSAT's product pages render by JavaScript and could not be listed.
**Village destruction over time.** Beyond the Marinka narrative there is no settlement-level damage time series. Sentinel-1 coherence methods exist but were not applied.

**Dataset corrections to the brief.** No EuroCrops Ukraine subset exists. FTW and AI4Boundaries exclude Ukraine. The Microsoft footprint licence is inconsistent (CDLA-P 2.0 in the repo vs ODbL at Overture).

**Process note.** The web-search quota ran out, so later research used OpenAlex, publisher site searches, the DeepState endpoints, Overpass, Microsoft footprints and EOX tiles. ISW pages returned 403. The procgen literature on field patterns and hedgerows is still thin.

**ISW's methodology page** still returns 403, and the Wayback copy of the 26 Sep 2026 ROCA does not repeat the "furthest assessed extent" sentence. That wording rests on pass-1 search excerpts. ISW's historic 2022 legend (e.g., "Ukrainian counteroffensives" on static maps) was not checked visually.

**November 2025 and 2024-total mismatches.** DeepState was quoted at "some 630" km² for November 2025 and 3,600+ km² for 2024, against 503 and 3,301 computed. May 2026 also has conflicting DeepState quotations (14 net per RFE/RL; 130 lost and 250 regained per Kyiv Post). DeepState's own Telegram monthly posts, which would settle these, were not fetched.

**Event-dated series.** The computed series follows publication dates. Reassigning OPSEC-delayed Ukrainian gains (e.g., Vivaldi, May–June 2026) to their event months would need DeepState's changelog text parsed per settlement.

**Suriyak's legend and cadence** are known only from editors' descriptions. Its maps are images on X and Telegram (X was not fetchable). Andrew Perpetua's map data file did not load outside the web app, so its polygon legend (as opposed to its event badges) is unverified.
**Liveuamap's legend** is not documented by the site. The side-colour reading comes from 19 captured events, and the live site blocks fetches.
**UA Control Map** legend and terms are unverified (the site returned only a 226-byte redirect stub).
**NYT "Maps: Tracking the Russian Invasion"** is blocked directly and through the Wayback Machine. Its methodology is unknown. The Kyiv Independent map pages were not fetched.
**DeepState's official terms of use** were not found. It is unclear whether the `/api/history/*` endpoints are tolerated for third-party use, so ask before any bulk use.
**Delta's visual design** (basemap, symbol set, colours) is not described in any fetched source. The NATO ACT "DELTA at CWIX24" article is still behind a Cloudflare challenge.
**Thermal and FPV visuals.** No source was found on which palette Ukrainian units prefer, or on analogue "signal loss" artefacts under EW. FLIR's palette guides are behind Cloudflare.
**GeoConfirmed commercial use** is not addressed by its API terms. Written permission is needed before shipping any of its data.
**Date conflict:** the Makarivka encirclement dispute is dated December 2024 by dev.ua. A Wikipedia summary placed it in December 2023. dev.ua's date is used.

**CSIS wargames on Russia–Ukraine or NATO–Russia**: not found. csis.org returns 403. The archived Futures Lab page lists Ukraine analysis (an energy-truce piece) but no Russia–Ukraine wargame, and PAXsims only references CSIS's Taiwan games. The NATO–Russia games that were found are German, British and Canadian (§5).

**Dstl on Ukraine drone lessons**: the gov.uk search API found only the Dstl–Slitherine case study, the Defence Wargaming Centre pages and a strategic-communications game (Defending Defender). No Ukraine drone game was public.

**Commercial FPV sims in Ukrainian schools**: no first-party source names Liftoff, VelociDrone, Uncrashed or DCL. Searches of Euromaidan Press's archive for each name found nothing. Only the vendor claim [src:vgi9-2025-drone-simulators] remains, and the verified military sims are all domestic.

**Combat Mission: Black Sea community mods** for FPV or 2022 content: the Battlefront forums returned 403. Official content was checked via the Steam news API, and none has shipped [src:steam-2023-cmbs-update-2-18].

**Developer countries still unverified**: Sand Table Software (the store page and the studio site give none), Bird's Eye Games (Regiments), Cats Who Play (Gostomel Heroes), Ravens Row (Hell Of War) and Battlestate Games (Escape from Tarkov). Death From Above's makers are confirmed German.
**ADB values before April 2025** beyond the infantry price, and the exact date of the 6→12 repricing, which falls between April 2025 and January 2026.
Why *Gostomel Heroes* is missing from the Ukrainian and German Steam stores (regional withdrawal, rating or developer choice) is not established.
The *Play for Ukraine* full text (Taylor & Francis) returns 403. Only its abstract and metadata were read.

**Total losses.** No reliable totals for the Battle of Kyiv exist (MWI) [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. No count of vehicles destroyed on the convoy road was found. Oryx (`oryx-russian-equipment-losses`) has no breakdown by road, and its aircraft list gives no places [src:oryx-2022-aircraft-losses-list].
**No km² figure** for the ground regained in the north was found. Note that the KB source `kyivpost-2022-60-settlements` is about Kherson, not Kyiv.
**Who destroyed the Mriya**, and exactly when between 24 and 27 Feb, is not established [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-an225-chief-pilot].

**Aerorozvidka.**
  - The claim is the commander's own and was not independently verified [src:guardian-2022-borger-aerorozvidka-convoy]. It is undated and located only "near Ivankiv".
  - **The KB claim 05-0009-02 reverses the order.** The Guardian original has the lead vehicles first, then the supply depot. Defense Express's rewrite put the depot first [src:defenseexpress-2022-aerorozvidka-convoy].
  - Pavliuk's "30 SSO soldiers" disabling the lead three vehicles is probably the same action [src:ukrinform-2023-pavliuk-30-sof].
**The tyre theory** (cheap tyres, poor maintenance) is carried only by the BBC and a Wikipedia relay of Forbes [src:bbc-2022-why-convoy-stopped] [src:wikipedia-2026-russian-kyiv-convoy].

**Units, unconfirmed.**
  - The 98th VDV Division's presence.
  - The 155th Naval Infantry at Moshchun, which rests on Ukrainian identifications.
  - Which unit died at Vokzalna.
  - The numbers of the "two artillery brigades" in Kyiv and of the TDF brigades other than the 112th.

**Makariv.** Credit for the 2 Mar recapture is contested: the 14th Mechanised (ISW) or the 95th Air Assault (MWI) [src:isw-2022-03-02-roca] [src:mwi-2025-collins-spencer-battle-of-kyiv]. The town was a "gray zone" again on 25 Mar [src:wikipedia-2026-battle-of-makariv].
**The Moshchun hold-or-withdraw exchange** is dated about 14 Mar by most sources and 21 Mar by SWJ.
**Air losses near Kyiv** could not be placed. The Su-27 crash street of 25 Feb and the S-400 attribution for Oksanchenko are unconfirmed.

**Unfetched sources.**
  - ISW warning updates for 28 Feb, 1 Mar and 29 Mar.
  - The NYT Bucha investigations: the satellite analysis of 4 Apr and the 234th Regiment piece of Dec 2022.
  - The OHCHR primary reports, so the figure of 73 comes via Wikipedia.
  - Forbes on the tyres, Reuters on the convoy, the DoD statements of 16 and 31 Mar, and WaPo's 30 Mar Moshchun report.

**Launch time.** 14:10 (Butusov) or about 16:00 (UP) [src:pravda-2023-pohorilov-neptune-launch-video] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune]. The firing position is given only as "south of Odesa Oblast" or "the coast between Odesa and Mykolaiv" [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune] [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva]. No coordinates.
**The Neptune unit and crew.** No Ukrainian source names them. Only a Russian court names the 406th Artillery Brigade [src:rbcukraine-2026-court-moskva]. Launcher count on 13 Apr unknown.
**TB2 role on 13 Apr.** Unresolved: UP contradicts itself between Nov and Dec 2022 [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
**US role in finding the target.** Unresolved. NYT's Mar 2025 "The Partnership" was not fetched [src:ukranews-2025-herasimova-navy-moskva-rescue].
***Moskva* losses.** Range from 1 to about 450, and the CO's fate is disputed. Treat as unknowable.

**The May assault.** The date (7 May vs. the night of 8–9 May), the helicopter mix and the losses (the *Stanislav*?) are inconsistent across UP, Zavhorodnii and Wikipedia. Bedzai's death on 7 May suggests 7 May [src:ppu-2024-bedzai].
**Raptors.** How many Raptors were lost at the island is unclear (2 + 2, or 2 + 3). Oryx's war-wide total is 3 destroyed and 2 damaged [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses].

**Who said the line.** Contested. The Guardian has border guard Roman Hrybov [src:guardian-2022-sauer-hrybov-medal]; Ukrposhta calls him "Marine Roman Grybov" [src:ukrposhta-2022-warship-stamp]; UP says it was an unnamed border guard, not Hrybov [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].

**Garrison count and prisoner ledger.** 80 vs 82, and 28 vs "about 30" border guards. The ledger from 19 (Mar), plus 1 (29 Oct), plus 3 (24 Nov), through 40 by Apr 2023, to the last on 23 Jul 2025 is incomplete.
**Russian garrison.** Its size and units on the island were never established.
**Light.** Sunrise and sunset times for the key days weren't sourced (the timeanddate.com fetch was blocked); add them from an astronomical table.
**The *Moskva*'s track** on 12–13 Apr before the strike, and the Boiko-tower coordinates, have no fetched source.
***Admiral Essen*.** The claimed Neptune strike date conflicts: 2 Apr (Russian court) vs 4 Apr (Ukrainian claim via Forbes).

**Air-bridge dates.** Only mission 1 (21 Mar), mission 3 (28 Mar) and the last flight (5 Apr, per Serbov) are dated. Missions 2, 4, 5 and 6 are not. TWZ's "around the middle of May" for the last sorties conflicts with the 5 Apr account and with GUR's figure of seven missions [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue] [src:rbc-2026-honcharova-serbov-interview].

**Helicopter losses.**
  - Counts differ: 2 shot down plus a rescue helicopter (Budanov) [src:twz-2022-altman-mariupol-helicopter-missions]; 1 destroyed and 2 "missing" officially (Flint) [src:twz-2022-altman-flint-helicopter-rescue]. Time describes two Mi-8s damaged on mission 6 that crash-landed on friendly ground [src:time-2024-spencer-collins-mariupol-helicopters].
  - Crew deaths are unknown: Zelensky said 90% of the pilots did not return [src:pravda-2022-mazurenko-azovstal-weapons-delivery], while Time documents no crew deaths.
  - Wikipedia's "six helicopters shot down overall" is unsourced here [src:wikipedia-siege-of-mariupol].
**Distance error.** Time's "82 km" from Dnipro to Mariupol is wrong; the straight-line distance is about 233 km [src:osm-nominatim-c03-places].
**FAB-3000.** Use against Azovstal is reported but not confirmed by Ukrainian or Western sources fetched for this dossier.
**Garrison numbers.** The strength at Azovstal by date, killed in action, and the size of each unit are not documented in Ukrainian primary sources reviewed here.

**Civilians.** The number of civilians in the plant is uncertain ("hundreds" to about 1,000). The total civilians evacuated from Azovstal across both operations is unclear; the UP total of about 567 includes people from the wider city.
**Russian losses** are only claimed (6,500 killed, per Ukraine).

**Olenivka toll:** 50+ (UN, 2023), 51 (UN, Oct 2023), 54 (RFE/RL), 57 (Kyiv Independent) [src:un-news-2023-olenivka-justice] [src:kyivpost-2023-afp-olenivka-not-himars] [src:rferl-2025-peretiatko-azovstal-captivity] [src:kyivindependent-2024-shulzhenko-kozatskyi].
**Drone footage.** Azov drone footage of the burning plant (early May) circulated widely, but no original upload or dated, stable URL was confirmed for this dossier.
**Geography.** The helicopter landing spots, the bunker locations and the internal layout (which shops, which tunnels) are not mapped in public sources found.
**Weather.** Values are reanalysis, not station records.
**Not yet consulted.** Ukrainian parliamentary or journalistic investigations of why the city was encircled so fast (raised by Serbov) [src:rbc-2026-honcharova-serbov-interview].
**Ammunition and launchers in the south.** No source gives the number of GMLRS rockets fired at the Kherson crossings or how many launchers were allotted to OC South.

**Date of the first bridge strike.** ISW reports 19 July [src:isw-2022-07-19-roca], while Miller gives 20 July in one article and implies 19 July in the other [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far].

**Was the road bridge ever reopened?** Wikipedia says repairs were completed by 23 August. Satellite imagery two days later showed 16 holes and ferries in use [src:wikipedia-antonivka-road-bridge] [src:isw-2022-08-29-roca].

**VDV composition.** Miller says the whole VDV except the 106th Division was on the right bank, while ISW names the 106th among the withdrawing units [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:isw-2022-11-09-roca]. The ORBAT figures come from open sources and Ukrainian claims, and are partly unverified.
**Size of the Russian force and of the withdrawal.** Estimates range from 20,000 to 42,370 (see section 1).
**Equipment losses.** There is no Kherson-specific Oryx-type count of equipment destroyed or abandoned in July–November, or of the trophies taken in November.
**Ukrainian losses.** Ukraine has never published figures. Only unit-level anecdotes and Russian claims exist.
**Date of the strike on the 247th Regiment and Chornobaivka.** The sources give 22 or 23 August [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].

**Did weather force the withdrawal?** Miller argues that winter ice would have stopped ferries, but ERA5 shows no daily minimum below 0 °C through 15 November [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:openmeteo-era5-kherson-2022]. Treat the freeze as a looming threat, not a fact of the window.

**Paywalled sources not checked first-hand.** The Washington Post (29 Dec 2022) and NYT (Entous, 29 Mar 2025) accounts of the planning, Kovalchuk's dam test and his dismissal are cited only through Wikipedia's summary of them.
**Coordinates.** The Darivka bridge itself was not geolocated; only the village centre is given. An Overpass query failed.

**Pier geometry.** The total number of piers, the pier numbering origin, typical span lengths per section (only the 64 m replacement span is sourced) and pier coordinates for supports 145 and 235–236 are not in any source used. A figure of 595 supports appeared only in search snippets and could not be tied to an acceptable source, so it was not used.

**Barrier dimensions.** Boom heights, net mesh, mine positions and the exact standoff distance from the bridge are unpublished. The spacing of the 2023 block ships is given as 160 m (UK DI), just over 0.1 mi (TWZ) or about 200 m (Militarnyi). Their direction is given as "south" (TWZ, UK DI) or "western approaches" (Sutton's post).
**Barge counts** swing with storms and reporting: 7 sections (May 2024), 21 in a second line (Jun), 30+ (Jul), 36 (Oct), 17 (Jan 2025). No clean time series.

**Act 1 charge.** The SBU says 21 t TNT equivalent of RDX; the Russian case file says about 10 t TNT equivalent of rocket fuel in 22.7 t of cargo. Spans down: 2 (case file) or 3 damaged with 2 down (Wikipedia). The explosion site is described three ways (§3).
**Act 2 launch point, route, range and endurance** of the Sea Babies are not disclosed. Neither is whether the CNN "road" and "rail" impacts struck the same pier group.

**Act 3 damage** is not independently verified. Reuters confirmed only the location [src:reuters-2025-polityuk-underwater]. The delivery method (divers, UUV, agents) is unknown, and Malyuk's "two × 1,100 kg" adds to the initial "1,100 kg".
**Unverified Russian claims:** whether the Aug–Sep 2023 and Aug 2024 attacks on the bridge happened as Russia described them.
**Weather** comes from ERA5 reanalysis, not station observations, and gives no sea state or visibility.
**Ukrainian losses and strength.** No figures were found for casualties, total troops, brigade strengths or vehicle numbers.
**Russian strength on 6 Sep.** Only fragments exist: the Balakliia force's percentages, and an Izium grouping of about 9,000–10,000. Total Russian personnel losses exist only as claims.

**The precise area for 6–12 Sep.** ISW's daily figures stop at "over 3,000 km²". The 6,000 and 8,000 km² figures mix the south and later days. A DeepState-based computation for 6–13 Sep only, inside Kharkiv Oblast, would settle it; it was not run here.

**Date conflicts.**
  - Balakliia: 8 Sep (ISW) against formal control on 10 Sep (Wikipedia).
  - Izium: 10 Sep (Wikipedia, WaPo) against 11 Sep (ISW geolocation).
  - Kharkiv Oblast "completely liberated" on 4 Oct (NGU), against 6% still occupied on 27 Sep (Syniehubov) and Russian presence east of the Oskil afterwards.
**The start line.** Pryshyb (Wikipedia, about 9 km NW of Balakliia by OSM, not the 15 km stated) or Andriivka for the 92nd.

**Unit roles.** The roles of the 3rd and 4th Tank Brigades and of Kraken rest on Wikipedia citing Hauer and Butusov; they need primary confirmation. HUR and SSO actions are almost undocumented in English.

**Not fetched.**
  - The Forbes (Axe) pieces on 4th GTD tank losses and the "10,000 surrounded" story returned 403, so they are cited only via Wikipedia.
  - The CNN source of the "338" Oryx figure was not fetched.
  - The FT interactive did not render without JavaScript.
**The Ukrainian reasoning for halting at the Oskil** is not documented in the sources found. Only Reznikov's caution and ISW's "if they choose" are available.
**Rail detail.** Exact Russian railheads and their daily throughput in Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi and Izium before the attack are unknown.
**Weather** is ERA5 reanalysis, not station data. There are no sources on fog or visibility for 6 Sep.

**Ukrainian losses** are the weakest number. Three counts should not be merged [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons] [src:meduza-2024-75000-dead] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-bakhmut]:
  - RUSI: about 10,000 killed or severely wounded.
  - UALosses (2024): about 4,600–5,500 named dead.
  - Wikipedia citing UALosses (2026): 14,235 killed and 16,569 missing, unchecked.

**The Ukrainian order of battle is incomplete.**
  - No dated Ukrainian-outlet confirmation was found for the 24th, 30th, 60th, 71st or 4th Tank brigades inside the city. They come from Forbes' December list [src:forbes-2022-axe-eight-brigades].
  - The International Legion's role rests only on Wikipedia [src:wikipedia-battle-of-bakhmut].
  - At Soledar only the 46th and 77th Airmobile are officially confirmed. The 61st and 10th Mountain Assault brigades, often named there, were not verified [src:president-2023-zelensky-soledar-46-77].

**The Soledar withdrawal date** is contested. The Kyiv Independent analysis puts the last Ukrainians out around 12 Jan, but official confirmation came on 25 Jan [src:kyivindependent-2023-ponomarenko-loss-of-soledar] [src:kyivindependent-2023-soledar-withdrawal-confirmed].

**Which road is "the road of life"** differs by source: the T0504 via Ivanivske, or the Khromove road (O0506) [src:businessinsider-2023-baker-jankowicz-unyielding-city] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-bakhmut-flanks-hold].
**Who blew the Khromove bridge** on 3 Mar is unresolved: Ukraine's own demolition or a Russian strike [src:isw-2023-03-04-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-kossov-bakhmut-troops-not-protected].

**Location gaps.**
  - AZOM's internal layout and the "underground sections" Wagner assaulted are not described in any fetched source [src:isw-2023-03-13-roca].
  - The MiG-17 monument and "the last high-rise" were not found as OSM features [src:osm-2026-bakhmut-geodata].

**Fire-rate figures** disagree by an order of magnitude between US and Ukrainian estimates (5,000 against 20,000 Russian rounds a day in January 2023) [src:cnn-2023-bertrand-russian-artillery-down-75].

**The size of the May strip** is reported three ways: 3 km × 2.6 km (Biletskyi), 2 km × 0.5 km (Prigozhin) and 1,730 m × 700 m (the 3rd Assault Brigade, later) [src:pravda-2023-3rd-assault-72nd-flees] [src:ukrinform-2023-3rd-assault-700m].
**Missing analyses.** No UNOSAT damage assessment for Bakhmut was found, and Planet imagery was not examined [src:reuters-2023-zafra-mcclure-bakhmut-destruction-analysis].
**Missing ISW dailies.** Several dailies (December 2022; 4 Feb, 15 and 31 Mar, 2 Apr, 6 Jun 2023) could not be fetched. The 20 December visit and December fighting rest on other sources.
**Unverified tactical claims.** The CNN-published Ukrainian intelligence report on Wagner tactics is single-source [src:cnn-2023-lister-wagner-tactics-report].

**No Oryx list for Vuhledar alone.** Oryx's master list [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses] does not tag locations. The only Oryx-derived figure found covers Avdiivka and Vuhledar together for 8–10 Feb [src:insider-2023-oryx-103-vehicles].
  - Wikipedia cites WarSpotting at "107+ armoured vehicles (17+ tanks)" for the whole 2022–24 battle [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar]. This was not checked directly, and a location-filtered WarSpotting export would settle it.

**The Ukrainian order of battle is thin.** The roles of the 68th Jaeger Brigade and the Kalinouski Regiment rest on Wikipedia's citations of the Washington Post [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar]. Battalion dispositions, artillery numbers, RAAM rounds fired, and minefield extents and locations are not public.

**Ukrainian personnel losses for Jan–Mar 2023 are unknown.** Wikipedia cites a Times figure for Sep 2022, a CBC figure for one battalion, and BBC Ukrainian name counts, none of them checked [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar].

**Exact dates of the iconic videos.** The "second column on the same route" video and the 13+12 engagement can be dated only to early February from their posting dates [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade] [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca]. GeoConfirmed's geolocations could give exact positions.

**The Ka-52 claims** (5–6 shot down on 24–28 Jan) and the strike on a building of reinforcements at "Kyrylivka" come via Tom Cooper's blog, relayed by Wikipedia. They are unverified [src:wikipedia-battle-of-vuhledar].
**Sergey Polyakov's** death and brigade are reported only by unofficial Russian sources via CNN [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys].

**The size of the 155th** before the battle is disputed: about 2,000 (Kyiv Post) against 5,000 (Ukrainian spokesman) [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines] [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade].
**The "Pivdennodonbaska No. 3"** mine near Vodiane needs matching to its OSM feature [src:isw-2024-09-30-roca] [src:osm-copyright].
**Not examined:** satellite imagery of the battlefield (Sentinel-2 or commercial) and the UK MoD image itself.

**The 8 June date and time.** DeepState dates the filmed column to the afternoon of 7 Jun. ISW, Romanchuk and Forbes date the breach to the night of 7–8 Jun and 8 Jun [src:euromaidan-2023-shandra-leopards-mala-tokmachka] [src:isw-2023-06-08-roca] [src:censor-2023-forbes-25-vehicles]. These may be two different episodes. An exact geolocation of the column ("about 4 km" or "roughly 2 miles" south of Mala Tokmachka) was not found [src:guardian-2023-beaumont-wintour-mala-tokmachka] [src:popularmechanics-2023-roblin-minefield-losses].

**Paywalled originals.** Forbes (David Axe's 25-vehicle count, the 120→500 m minefield story, the 518-vehicle Zaporizhzhia tally), the Washington Post (4 Dec 2023), the NYT ("The Partnership", 2025) and Reuters could not be fetched. They appear only through Censor.NET, Euromaidan Press, the Kyiv Independent and Wikipedia [src:censor-2023-forbes-25-vehicles] [src:euromaidan-2023-wp-analysis] [src:wikipedia-2023-ukrainian-counteroffensive].

**No area figure for the salient alone.** Ukrainian MoD figures (256.5–260 km²) cover the whole south [src:kyivindependent-2023-court-4-8-km2] [src:kyivindependent-2023-khalilova-vdv-robotyne]. A DeepState polygon difference for the Orikhiv box between 4 Jun and 30 Nov would settle it [src:deepstate-api-history].

**Markus's protest date.** Ukrainska Pravda dates his demotion request to 11 Jul. The Kyiv Independent writes "June 11", and a later Pravda note says "11 September" [src:pravda-2023-markus-demotion] [src:kyivindependent-2023-farrell-47th-surovikin-line] [src:pravda-2023-sak-removed].

**Distances.** Outlets give Robotyne as 10–20 km from Orikhiv and Verbove as 9–20 km from Robotyne. OSM gives 15.0 km and 12.5 km [src:isw-2023-07-26-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2023-ostiller-verbove-breakthrough] [src:osm-overpass-2026-c09-places].

**Ukrainian personnel losses.** No reliable axis figure was found. The 47th's "2,000 of 5,000" rests on El País via Wikipedia. UALosses-type name counts were not examined [src:wikipedia-2023-ukrainian-counteroffensive].

**Oryx counts by date.** Oryx's list carries no locations or dates. The window figures come from press snapshots of it [src:oryx-ukrainian-losses] [src:popularmechanics-2023-roblin-minefield-losses]. WarSpotting gives Russian losses only [src:warspotting-api-russian-losses].

**Brigade roles.** The 65th's role in taking Robotyne, the Skelia battalion and the 118th Brigade are named in secondary sources but not confirmed here [src:wikipedia-2023-ukrainian-counteroffensive].
**The Russian commanders after Lyamin**, and the 810th's actual losses, are unconfirmed [src:isw-2023-10-10-roca] [src:wikipedia-2023-ukrainian-counteroffensive].
**Not examined:** Sentinel-2 imagery of the minefields and trench lines, and the NYT interactive on Robotyne (20 Sep 2023).

**Exact withdrawal date.** "Several weeks" before 16 Jul 2024 (Suspilne). The last reported ground combat was on 11 Jul. Wikipedia uses 17 Jul. No official date exists [src:euromaidan-2024-tril-krynky-withdraw] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-retreat].

**Ukrainian losses.** Official figures are a state secret. There is no breakdown of losses on the river versus in the village, or by brigade beyond "about 700" for one. The UALosses captured count is 54 or 64 [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-krynky].

**Russian losses after November 2023.** Only Lykhovii's ratio and Naalsio's equipment count exist. The November claim is variously printed as 1,216 or 1,126 KIA, and as 14 "watercraft", "boats" or "aircraft" [src:euromaidan-2023-zoria-marines-bridgeheads] [src:isw-2023-11-17-roca] [src:isw-2023-12-16-roca] [src:kyivindependent-2024-ostiller-krynky-lost]. The boats reading fits the Marine Corps release.

**The Antonivskyi footholds.** Mashovets's 9 Nov claim of continuous control from the rail bridge to the road bridge conflicts with UP's account that both western footholds were abandoned by early November. A March 2024 return to the road bridge is reported only by Russian bloggers and Saldo [src:isw-2023-11-09-roca] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold] [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-krynky-drones].
**Boat types and counts.** No full inventory: hulls, motors and losses per month. "US boats with pontoons" is not identified by model.
**Russian strength figures** (64k → 120k) are expert estimates with no stated method.
**Weather.** Fog days and river state (current, ice) were not sourced. The temperatures are modelled.
**Timing of the raids before Krynky.** The Feb–Jun 2023 island raids and the unit roles in the summer raids are thinly documented. The best sources are UP and KI soldier testimony.
**The parliamentary follow-up.** It is not known whether the defence committee ever held the hearing Bobrovska proposed.
**Chemical weapons.** Testimony only, with no OPCW finding sourced here.

**Zenit's coordinates.** The base is not tagged in OSM. Its position is known only as "1–2 km south" of the city, east of Opytne, near the "Cheburashka" crossroads on the Donetsk ring road [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka] [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka]. Descriptions also disagree on whether it is "southeastern" or "south-western" [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-zenit-withdrawal].

**The date the terrikon fell.** Russian claims run from 12 Oct to 28 Oct, ISW saw no full control by either side on 26 Oct, and Kremlin channels claimed it again in late November [src:isw-2023-10-12-roca] [src:isw-2023-10-26-roca] [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-factory-district]. Who held it in October is also contested: the 129th TD per Kyiv Post, the 110th per Euromaidan Press [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-worst-defeat-avdiivka] [src:euromaidan-2023-avdiivka-spoil-tip].
**The 3rd Assault's arrival** ranges from 3 to 15 Feb (section 2), and its mission is disputed (section 7).

**Ukrainian losses.** No official Ukrainian count of the whole battle or of the withdrawal exists in these sources. The 850–1,000 figure (NYT) versus about 100 (US officials via WaPo) is unresolved [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].

**The pipe's dimensions and route** conflict across sources: 0.5 m and 2 km, 1.3–1.4 m, or 3.7 km [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka] [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-last-days-avdiivka] [src:united24-2026-kabachynskyi-pipelines]. The entry and exit points are not geolocated here.
**KAB counts** come from units and milbloggers. There is no single series, and the UK MoD's 30–50 a day reaches us only through Wikipedia [src:wikipedia-battle-of-avdiivka].

**Kyiv Post's "25th Combined Arms Army" for the October assault** conflicts with ISW's 8th CAA and 1st AC [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-worst-defeat-avdiivka] [src:isw-2023-10-11-roca]. LWJ places 25th CAA vehicles there only later [src:lwj-2024-hardie-avdiivka-analysis].
**Satellite imagery** of the destroyed plant and the city was not found in this pass. Commercial imagery (Maxar, Planet) is not cited here.
**Pre-battle shell stocks**, and the actual number of tubes and drones with each Ukrainian brigade, are not in these sources.

**Which weapon on 14 January.** A US officer's public statement (Patriot) is the strongest attribution [src:twz-2024-newdick-patriot-a50-confirmed]. Ukraine never officially named the system for the first kill, and the friendly-fire claim persists in Russian sources. Was the Il-22M hit by the same battery? The exact missile type (PAC-2 GEM-T or other) is unconfirmed.
**Positions and ranges.** No source gives the aircraft's coordinates at the moment of the hit. Range claims run from 160 to 300 km (§3). The time zone of HUR's 18:45 is unstated.

**Identities and crews.** The 14 Jan aircraft is RF-93966 in Militarnyi, Wikipedia and ASN but "RF-50601" in Euromaidan [src:euromaidanpress-2024-zoria-a50-azov]. The 23 Feb identity (RF-50610) rests on a search-only ASN listing. The 14 Jan death toll runs from 11 to about 15.

**Fleet baseline and what remains.** The counts are mutually inconsistent (§1). Spiderweb's A-50 damage is imaged but not quantified. The 2026 refurbished A-50U may be a returned airframe rather than a new one [src:theaviationist-2026-satam-new-a50u].

**The Times's S-300 bait account.** It is known here only through Babel's summary [src:babel-2024-perepechko-times-a50]; the original article is paywalled and was not read. It is unclear which engagements the bait tactic applied to.

**The "May 2024 Patriot ambushes on Su-34s and Ka-52s near the border".** No such event was found in Ukrainian or Western sources. The well-documented border Patriot ambush is **13 May 2023** over Bryansk (Su-34, Su-35, three Mi-8s) [src:liga-2023-dzheripa-bryansk-patriot]. The 2024 Patriot-linked Su-34 losses found are 22 Dec 2023 (south, suspected), the February 2024 spree (system not stated), and 1 Nov 2024 (Belgorod, a milblogger's guess) [src:kyivpost-2023-struck-feshchenko-three-su34] [src:kyivpost-2024-orlova-six-aircraft-72h] [src:kyivpost-2024-su34-two-majors]. The 2024 Ka-52 losses seen in search were to MANPADS, not Patriot. This needs a targeted pass if the chapter wants a 2024 helicopter ambush.
**Machulishchy damage.** It is attested only by the partisans and by Lukashenko's eventual admission; the imagery was inconclusive [src:ukrinform-2023-machulishchy-satellite].
**Weather.** Values are reanalysis, not station observations. Cloud base and the moon's altitude were not checked.

**Kyiv 2022 numbers.** Air-to-air kill counts are uncertain because of overclaiming on both sides [src:rusi-2022-bronk-russian-air-war]. Tarabalka's date of death differs between sources (13 vs 23 March).

**Launch points and transit routes** are undisclosed. Budanov declined to say whether a mothership was used [src:twz-2024-altman-ivanovets]. There are no sourced coordinates for the strike positions apart from the place names (Donuzlav raid, 4 km off Alupka, 5 km off Cape Takil, about 50 km west of Novorossiysk).
**Times** of the 2024 sinkings and of the air kills are not given to the hour, apart from the 2022 and 2023 Russian claims.

**The Olenegorsky Gornyak drone** is contested: Malyuk says Sea Baby, HUR says the SBU's Mamai [src:wikipedia-sea-baby][src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate]. Oryx's naval list does not appear to include the ship (our reading of the page) [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses].
**Which ships were hit on 29 Oct 2022** beyond the *Makarov* and *Ivan Golubets* is unknown. Ukrainian channels said four [src:wikipedia-2022-sevastopol-drone-attack].

**The Serna and Akula fate.** HUR says destroyed. Oryx lists one Serna destroyed, one Serna damaged and one Ondatra damaged, without dates in the list text [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate][src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses].
**The second Mi-8 and second Su-30** have no public visual confirmation. We could not identify a 2–3 May 2025 Su-30SM entry in Oryx [src:oryx-russian-equipment-losses].
**The type of the R-73-armed boat** in the May 2024 Ka-29 video is unclear: Sea Baby per Wikipedia, Magura per The Aviationist [src:wikipedia-sea-baby][src:aviationist-2024-durso-magura-mi8].
**Kyiv Independent coverage** could not be fetched (a client-rendered page), so the chapter leans on UP, EMP and Ukrinform for the Ukrainian voice.

**Post-window coda for another chapter:** Sea Baby strikes on tankers off Turkey (Nov 2025) and the underwater Sea Baby against a submarine at Novorossiysk (Dec 2025) [src:kyivindependent-2025-zadorozhnyy-kairos-virat][src:kyivindependent-2025-myronyshena-sub-sea-baby].

**Peak area actually controlled.** No independent final figure. ISW's 800 km² is *claimed* extent as of 12 Aug. Ukrainian numbers (1,000–1,300 km²) are unverified. DeepState's history API excludes Russian territory [src:isw-2024-08-12-roca; src:deepstate-api-history].

**Ukrainian strength and losses.** The force estimates range from 2,000 at the start (OSW) to 12,000 (Western) to "at most 30,000" (ISW). No official casualty figures exist; only UALosses via Wikipedia [src:osw-2024-wilk-kursk-action; src:bbc-2025-beale-retreat-from-kursk; src:cnn-2025-edwards-russia-advancing-kursk; src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive].

**The pipeline force.** About 100 (Ukrainska Pravda) against "over 600" (Gerasimov). One unverified claim says 80% were killed at the exit [src:twz-2025-newdick-kursk-pipeline; src:nv-2025-romanenko-pipeline-ambush].

**Paywalled or blocked sources not used directly:** Forbes (Axe), Reuters, the Telegraph, WSJ and the FT. Their claims appear only via Wikipedia, where noted.
**The Oktyabrskoye toll.** Estimates of up to 200–500 casualties are analysts' estimates, unverified [src:kyivpost-2024-oktyabrskoye-himars; src:wikipedia-2024-kursk-offensive].

**Exact strike times.** No source fetched gives the launch minute at any base. The first reports were published from 10:52 UTC (§2), Barents calls it "Sunday morning", and TWZ "this afternoon" for Belaya. Whether the four launches were simultaneous in absolute time, and what local hour each was, remains open.

The Wikipedia/Baza and Kyiv Post/Baza dates for the company and the trucks (October versus December 2024) disagree. When and how the drones crossed into Russia, and from where (Kazakhstan has been speculated [src:euromaidanpress-2025-zoria-trojan-truck]), is unpublished.
**The drone and its payload.** Is it the *Osa* (Wikipedia), and is the payload 3.2 kg or 1.8 kg (WSJ)? Were there 150 drones and 300 munitions (Butusov)? Is 117 versus 116 a counting difference?
**The AI's role.** The only primary claim is the SBU's own statement [src:ssu-2025-pavutyna-video-41]. The Poltava museum training story is second-hand [src:kyivpost-2025-brown-ai-museum].

**Aircraft present.** Pre-strike counts conflict, especially at Olenya: 2 Tu-95MS on 26 May (AviVector) against a Russian media claim of 40 Tu-22M3 and 11 Tu-95MS. The Belaya breakdown does not add up (52 versus 48).

**Be-12.** The brief lists the Be-12 among the aircraft present. No source reviewed here reports a Be-12 at any Spiderweb base or among the aircraft hit. The SBU's own list is A-50, Tu-95, Tu-22, Tu-160, An-12 and Il-78 [src:ssu-2025-pavutyna-video-41].
**Tu-160 and Il-78 damage.** Both are claimed by the SBU, but no imagery confirms them. Analysts think the Tu-160 fleet is largely intact [src:wikipedia-operation-spiderweb].
**The A-50s.** At least one was hit on video. Whether either was operational, and whether the imagery shows new damage, is unresolved (§9).
**The Ukrainka failure.** Was it a wiring or charging fault, sabotage, or an accident? The WSJ says only that "something provoked a fire" [src:nv-2025-semenova-wsj-spiderweb].

**Not pursued here.** Claims of an Il-76 near Olenya and a Northern Fleet strike at Severomorsk were denied locally and not pursued. Bortnikov's later claim of British involvement appears only in non-English wikis and was not sourced here.
**Weather and light.** The values are reanalysis, not station observations, and are not tied to a strike hour.
**The exact exit points** near Radkivka are not published: UP shows only approximate points, and they changed regularly [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours].
**Length.** The quoted figures (10, more than 10, 15 km) depend on which endpoints are counted. Ours (10.5 km) rests on an OSM line whose naming looks wrong [src:osm-2026-kupiansk-pipeline-geodata].
**The date of the cut** (21 Oct per Butusov or 12 Dec per Khartiia) and the strength of the Russian force (40 to 500) are unresolved (see section 1).
**The 305 km²** in ISW's late-December figure may include ground beyond the immediate Kupiansk box. ISW gives no breakdown [src:isw-2026-02-15-roca].

**The 3 t demolition.** It is unclear whether it destroyed the river crossing or only one section, since a pipe that is "damaged in sections, not destroyed" was still in use in 2026 [src:defenseexpress-2025-achilles-pipeline-destroyed] [src:gwara-2026-diachenko-pipeline-damaged].
**Russian units that went through the pipe.** None is named in these sources; only "Veterans" specialists appear [src:kyivindependent-2026-terajima-kupiansk-pipelines].
**Ukrainian losses** for the operation are not published.

**Avdiivka pipe dimensions** conflict: 0.8 m and about 2 km in pro-Russian claims [src:kyivpost-2024-korshak-avdiivka-pipe], against 3.7 km and up to 1.4 m per United24 [src:united24-2026-kabachynskyi-pipelines].
**Jet versus piston drones.** The Air Force does not split the 496 drones by type. Neither the jet share nor the jet interception rate for this night is known [src:pravda-2026-romanenko-570-targets].

**Kill per layer.** No public breakdown by Patriot, IRIS-T, NASAMS, fighters, interceptor drones, mobile fire groups or EW. "Downed/suppressed" combines kills and jamming [src:isis-2026-anokhin-shahed-monthly]. F-16 and Mirage sorties that night are not reported.

**Count reconciliation.**
  - 28 ballistic launched, 4 downed, 25 "ballistic" hits; two Kh-101s unaccounted for [src:pravda-2026-romanenko-570-targets].
  - The MoD's 77 missiles against the Air Force's 74 [src:pravda-2026-bondarieva-fedorov-patriot-appeal].
  - Kh-101 launch areas: the Air Force says Vologda Oblast.

**Impact times and weapons per site.** No source maps each hit to a time and weapon, except "two missiles" in Darnytskyi (BBC) and the drone hit on the hotel (witness) [src:bbc-2026-rainsford-most-massive-kyiv][src:kyivindependent-2026-fenbert-kyiv-attack-31-killed].

**BBC time error.** BBC gives missiles at "01:00 (23:00 GMT)". Kyiv is UTC+3 in summer, and the Air Force's first missile alerts come at 01:53 [src:bbc-2026-rainsford-most-massive-kyiv][src:uaf-2026-kpszsu-alerts-1-2-july].

**Desnianskyi.** Klitschko reported a nine-storey collapse in Desnianskyi, but later DSNS and Ukrainska Pravda reporting places the collapse and the recovered bodies in Darnytskyi [src:kyivindependent-2026-fenbert-kyiv-attack-31-killed][src:pravda-2026-pohorilov-search-completed].

**Energy damage.** DTEK and Ukrenergo reported damage and outages in Kyiv without naming facilities, and no CHP is reported hit [src:kyivindependent-2026-fenbert-kyiv-attack-31-killed][src:pravda-2026-kryzhnyi-power-outages].
**Patriot battery count and sites** are not public. Nor is the size of the PAC-3/PAC-2 stock on 1 July.
**Russian targeting claims.** Which "military plants" were meant is unspecified, and there is no independent battle damage assessment of military targets in Kyiv.

**Start date.** Mid-April (Axe), May (MWI), late spring (KI York), and August counterattacks (Rybar). Kudriashov counts the stabilisation as the first phase [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-btr60-vbied] [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains] [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi].

**The July narrative.** Axe has Nove taken in July [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap]. Thorkill has July and early August attacks repelled by the 144th MRD until 17–18 Aug [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].
**Season 2 area.** 40 km² (Biletskyi as quoted by KI) or 50 km² (ISW). The 125 km² total implies 40 [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains] [src:isw-2026-09-20-roca].

**Losses do not add up.** About 1,500 (season 1) plus 800 (season 2) is not "more than 3,000" [src:hromadske-2026-lisova-vivaldi-phase1] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-murdoch-vivaldi-phase2]. Is the 2,000 of season 3 cumulative? Ukrainian losses are unpublished.
**The VBIED vehicle.** BTR-60 (corps and Euromaidan) or BTR-80 (ISW) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-btr60-vbied] [src:isw-2026-09-28-roca].

**DeepState lag.**
  - *No change before 14 Sep:* by our computation DeepState showed no change at all in the Vivaldi box from 1 Feb to 13 Sep [src:deepstate-api-history].
  - *Conflict with the KB:* this conflicts with the KB claim that May–June gains appeared in DeepState's August versions. They may lie outside our box, or the claim may refer to AMK's "OPSEC release" [src:amk-mapping-control-map].
  - *Still behind:* on 30 Sep DeepState still showed Kolodiazi and Zelena Dolyna as Russian, against ISW's 15 Sep reading and Thorkill's satellite confirmation [src:isw-2026-09-15-roca] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-240].

**Russian order of battle.** Which divisions were inside the salient: the 2nd and 144th (Axe), the "2nd and 14th" (MWI), or the 3rd and 144th (ISW)? Russian strength is unknown [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-salient-trap] [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:isw-2026-05-23-roca].
**Distance to Nove.** Sources say 15–16 km from Lyman, against 20.3 km between OSM centroids [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-lyman-holds] [src:osm-2026-vivaldi-geodata].
**The Starlink link.** It is indirect: no 3rd Corps statement ties Vivaldi to the cutoff [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
**Season 4** had not been announced by 30 Sep. Kudriashov's Ukrainska Pravda column is known only through TWZ and EUobserver [src:twz-2026-altman-vivaldi] [src:euobserver-2026-vasilko-vivaldi].
**Unfetched pages.** ATESH's rail claim is unverified [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-atesh-voronezh-rail]. The NV and ArmyInform interviews (Ukrainian-language) were not fetched.

**Aerorozvidka.** Its role is **not confirmed** by any source found. The footage was "released by the Ukrainian army" [src:nyt-2022-kramer-brovary-tanks] or HUR [src:interestingengineering-2022-brovary-convoy]. One drone blog claims a TB2 [src:dronedj-2022-crumley-brovary], which looks unfounded. Aerorozvidka's documented 2022 ambushes are on the north-western column [src:defenseexpress-2022-aerorozvidka-convoy].
  - *A Ukrainian-language lead:* Darmohrai's interview (Tyzhden, 2026-04-01, https://tyzhden.ua/oborona-brovariv-i-bytva-za-kyiv-iak-ukrainski-vijskovi-znyshchyly-tankovyj-polk-rf-interv-iu-z-romanom-darmohraiem/) says a battalion UAV operator directed the mortar battery's fire. It also tells of a forward ambush near Zalissia with NLAW and RPG-18, a Stuhna team with Chornovol, and a T-72B3 crew that escaped under its own smoke. It is not cited here because the brief requires English sources. Worth an English-language confirmation.
**The exact ambush point.** We give only OSM's Skybyn centre and the road geometry, and no geolocation of the clip from a source we fetched.
**Independent loss counts.** None found, for example from Oryx entries tied to this road.
**Zakharov.** No Russian-side confirmation in these sources.
**The 239th Tank Regiment.** Its presence rests on HUR's statement alone [src:interfax-2022-hur-brovary-zakharov].
**The exact date and place.** The only date is a Telegram channel's "Thursday" [src:newsweek-2024-cole-bradley-t90], and there is no geolocation.
**The identities.** The crew of the first Bradley, the full name of the second's crew, and the T-90M's unit are all unknown.
**The ammunition problem** the gunner mentions is not explained, and whether DU rounds were used is speculation by an expert [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].

**The Bradley record.**
  - *Losses:* Oryx counted at least 65 Bradleys lost by January 2024 [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts], and by April 2024 the 47th had lost at least 40 of its roughly 200 [src:wikipedia-2026-47th-mechanized-brigade].
  - *Kills:* there is no systematic count of Bradley kills against Russian armour at Avdiivka. The incidents above are anecdotal and drawn from video.
**The 21-tank day** rests on a single OSINT tally relayed by Forbes [src:forbes-2023-axe-21-tanks-stepove].
